title: Collation: one or many collation versions per data file
summary: Andrei Tserakhau (laskoviymishka) split one decision out of the collation thread and PR #16972: whether a data file may carry collation bounds for more than one collation version. Each bound is tagged with the version it was computed under, and a reader uses it only if it can reproduce that version; this affects pruning, not correctness. With a per-file list of {version, lower, upper}, a file written under one ICU version can be pruned by a reader on another once a bound for that version is added, for example by compaction, at the cost of a slightly larger stats struct. With one version per file, readers on another version cannot prune until the file is rewritten. He preferred multi-version. Alexander Loeser agreed and relayed a concern attributed to Russell about adding many fields to content_stats, with derived non-materialized fields as an alternative. Tserakhau prototyped both layouts and closed the thread: multi-version per file is settled, and how the bounds are stored continues in a new thread.

positions.stance: A data file should be able to carry bounds for several collation versions, because different ICU versions are live at the same time during upgrades.

Multi-version is preferable since a second set of metrics helps during ICU upgrades, but the storage format needs more discussion, including derived non-materialized fields that reuse lower_bounds and upper_bounds.

outcome.note: Multi-version collation bounds per data file is settled. How the bounds are stored, on top of stats-only fields, continues in a separate thread, and the planned October 28 sync was dropped.

why_it_matters: The decision fixes part of the on-disk metadata layout for collated columns and lets bounds for a new ICU version be added to existing files.
